patch.value: PmClient activation queue serializes unrelated workspaces and extension-free actions
GH-742: replace process-wide SDK activation serialization with request/workspace-scoped safety so independent embedded tenants can execute concurrently.

noExtensions built-in actions bypass global activation serialization; independent workspace/request registries execute concurrently without cross-request leakage; shared legacy global-state activation remains safely serialized or explicitly configured; deterministic concurrency tests prove both non-blocking and isolation; public SDK docs state the concurrency contract
Run a delayed PmClient action for workspace A concurrently with a built-in noExtensions list/get for workspace B; B waits behind the module-global activation queue.
Extension-free actions and independent workspace activation contexts execute concurrently while genuinely shared unsafe extension state remains isolated.
Every PmClient.run call enters one process-wide activation queue, coupling unrelated workspace latency and making each process single-flight.
Multi-user embedded hosts suffer cross-tenant head-of-line blocking and throughput bounded by one SDK action at a time per process.
